newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela April non-oil exports up 7 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela April non-oil exports up 7 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Venezuela's non-traditional exports, which exclude oil and iron, were up $23 million, or 6.7 percent, at $367 million in April, from $344 million in April 1996, the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI) said Thursday.
Exports for the first four months of the year, at $1.360 billion, were up $98 million, or 7.8 percent, from $1.262 billion in the same period last year, the OCEI figures showed.
Non-traditional exports fell $274 million, or 6.1 percent, to $4.213 billion in 1996.

"Common metals" was the strongest export sector in the first four months of 1997 with 37.4 percent of total exports. "Chemical products" came next with an 16.1 percent share, then "food, drinks and tobacco" with 8.2 percent.

The United States was the chief market for Venezuela's non-traditional exports with 27.6 percent. Venezuela's next largest export market was Colombia with a 25.2 percent share, followed by the Mexico with 4.0 percent, the Netherlands with 3.8 percent, Japan with 3.1 percent and the United Kingdom with 0.7 percent.
